title: ControlPlaneProductConfig
description: SPEC §8.1. The product-owned docs/delivery/plane.json read by `ccp`. Its presence is the product's opt-in to ccp. Every key but project_id has a plane default (ccp/config.py); unknown keys are refused. No secrets.

project_id.description: Same id as the plane binding; written into INDEX.yaml

statuses.description: Deprecated and not read: a task file's statuses are fixed, pending | done | dropped (SPEC §5)

refs_any.description: At least one of these frontmatter lists is non-empty

sections.description: `## <name>` headings every task carries: the canonical six by default (SPEC §5); a product may require more. `Context (not verified)` is read as `Context (not checked)`

kinds.description: SPEC §5.4, §20: per task kind, refs_any (the ref lists it cites at least one of; default the task log's refs_any) and forbid (ref lists it leaves empty). Read only with the architect block on

reviews_dir.description: Shaping and triage records (sh-*.md, ar-*.md), relative to dir (SPEC §19.6)

review_point_pattern.description: SPEC §22.1, §22: while the product keeps no review-point register, a task's `review_point` matches this and `ccp tasks close` stamps only a point that does. Once the register exists it is ignored, with a warning: review points are then R<n> and listed in the register.

index.description: SPEC §5.7: keep the generated INDEX.yaml (its format frozen), or none

dry_run.description: SPEC §21.1: ccp tasks check refuses a task not done or dropped whose dod_check has a step that runs a backticked command (`N. Run `...``) but neither a `dry run (`<sha>`):` line nor `dry run: n/a — <reason>`

claude_md_dirs.description: Directories documented by an auto-loaded CLAUDE.md instead of doc_name

language.description: SPEC §21: the language pack (ccp/doclang). It adds its source suffixes and directory names to the core's and runs its per-file checks over docstring_globs; none runs the language-neutral core alone

source_suffixes.description: null: the core's (.sql, .json, .md) plus the language pack's. A list replaces both

exempt_dirs.description: Directory names (any depth) or root-relative paths never judged. null: the core's plus the language pack's. A list replaces both

path_ref_suffixes.description: Backticked paths with these suffixes in a package doc must exist

docstring_globs.description: Root-relative globs of files that get the language pack's per-file checks (python: a module docstring)

no_delivery_ids.description: SPEC §21.3: no task, finding or ruling id in a package doc or in a code comment of a file under docstring_globs; false turns the check off

delivery_id_patterns.description: Regexes for the product's own ids (findings, rulings, tickets), checked beside the plane's

rules.description: SPEC §21.6: opt-in generic rules (ccp/docrules.py), each off until named

citations.description: Outside fenced code, every SPEC ref (ids.spec.prefix + number, .n subsections, ranges) in files under globs names a heading in a target doc; every [x](doc.md#anchor) link names an existing heading (GitHub anchors)

no_ids.description: No line of a file under globs carries a delivery id: by default task ids, zero-padded task numbers and 'task N' at the product's width; patterns (regexes) replace the defaults

history_attr.description: Git attribute marking history paths: the rules above skip them; ccp docs history-paths lists them

no_overlap.description: No two check commands (architect.checks, docs.checks) run the same command or the same test module

no_call_bullets.description: python pack: a module docstring does not list functions as backticked call bullets

docs.description: SPEC §21.5: product commands ccp docs check runs, not tied to a house rule

checks.description: Run in the product root by ccp docs check; exit 0 = pass

workers.description: How many check commands (docs.checks, and architect.checks) ccp docs check runs at once, each under its own timeout; results in declared order. 1 runs them one after another

architect.description: SPEC §8.1. Absent: the architect seat is off (no exit 4 at `ccp tasks next`, no shaping check, no rule checks). Every value is checked

rules_doc.description: Product path of the house rules, e.g. docs/ENGINEERING.md (template: templates/docs-project/ENGINEERING.md)

rules_max_lines.description: ccp docs check fails a longer rules doc

every_n_tasks.description: A pass is due once this many tasks are done since the last pass (operator, 2026-10-14)

max_days.description: Or this many days since the last pass, with at least one task done

notes_due.description: Or this many friction notes since the last pass

drift_ratio.description: Or the median wall time of the last 5 tasks is above this times the 10 before

grace_tasks.description: ccp tasks next exits 4 once a due pass is unstarted this many merges later

triage_grace_tasks.description: ccp tasks next exits 4 once a report has waited this many merges for triage

shape_adrs.description: ccp tasks check fails a pending task citing an ADR with no sh-*.md record (needs shape_from_task)

shape_from_task.description: Only tasks numbered from this one on are checked

refactor_every.description: After this many features merge since the last refactor, next returns a ready refactor first (0: off)

refactor_in_scope.description: deps: a refactor joins a scope only when a scope task depends on it, and the rest go to the top of the next review point's scope; true: every runner's scope; false: only a scope that names it (SPEC §20.4)

call_timeout_minutes.description: Wall-clock limit on the architect call

max_new_tasks.description: Cap on tasks one triage may create

probes.description: Read-only command prefixes the architect may run (each becomes Bash(<probe>:*))

checks.description: Product commands run by ccp docs check, so the verifier gates on them (exit 0 = pass)

budgets.description: ccp budgets over tracked files. Diagnostics: measured by `ccp architect due` (a breach makes a pass due) and `ccp health`, never by `ccp docs check`

metrics.description: Numbers ccp health record accepts besides the built-in suite series (suite_seconds, suite_tests and their _warm, _part and _unverified kinds, SPEC §27.2)

areas.description: Area name -> globs; ccp health splits each merge's files and lines by them

shape_only_dirs.description: Read for structure only; values never quoted

private_dirs.description: Denied to the architect's Read tool and named in its prompt

prompts.description: SPEC §13.2: the product's own rules for worker prompts, rendered after the plane template; SPEC §23.8: what the prompt audit keeps and for how long.

fragment.description: Product path of the fragment (e.g. docs/delivery/WORKERS.md).

worker_env.description: SPEC §13: NAME: template. `ccp prompt` renders each ({{run_id}}, {{task_id}}, {{nnnn}}, {{phase}}, {{worktree}}, {{main_checkout}}, {{queue_root}}, {{project_id}}) into the run's env file, which the prompt tells the worker to source in each command.

keep_body.description: SPEC §23.8: keep the full prompt text (prompt_body) in each prompt audit. Default false: the audit holds ids, refs and the prompt's sha256 and length.

audit_keep_days.description: SPEC §23.8: prompt audits (QUEUE_ROOT/prompts/**/<UTC>_<phase>.json) older than this many days, by the stamp in their name, are removed when `ccp prompt` writes an audit. Default null: all are kept.

reconcile.description: SPEC §10.5 `ccp tasks close`: the product's records beside the task file.

log.description: Prepend one entry to a product log. `entry` is a Python format string with date, task_id, nnnn, pr, head, head7, merge_sha, merge7, summary, review_point, title; it goes before the first line matching the regex `before` (or at the end).

hooks.description: Product commands run in the runner worktree, with TASK_ID, PR, HEAD_SHA, MERGE_SHA, SUMMARY and QUEUE_ROOT set. Their changes join the reconcile commit. A hook must be idempotent: a close re-run after a failure runs the hooks again.

adapter.description: Legacy (before SPEC §12): worktree_dir and worktree_links read as worktrees.dir and worktrees.links; post_close commands still run once at close. New products use worktrees and env.

worktree_dir.description: Where `ccp tasks claim` makes task worktrees, relative to the main checkout (impl-NNNN); reviewers and verifiers use rev-NNNN and ver-NNNN beside them.

worktree_links.description: Paths linked into each task worktree from the main checkout (e.g. .venv).

post_close.description: Commands `ccp tasks close` runs in the main checkout after the reconcile; {task_id} and {nnnn} are filled in. A failure is a warning.

worktrees.description: SPEC §12.1: where `ccp wt` makes worktrees and what it links into them.

dir.description: Relative to the main checkout; worktrees are named <kind>-<nnnn>[-<n>] (impl, rev, ver, mut, mac). Null: no plane-made worktrees.

links.description: Paths linked into each worktree from the main checkout (e.g. a virtualenv).

env.description: SPEC §12.1 env hooks: shell command templates run in the worktree. {task_id} {nnnn} {kind} {seat} {tag} {worktree} {main_checkout} {name} are filled in (other braces are literal) and also set as CCP_WT_<FIELD>.

setup.description: When a worktree is made; a failure removes it again.

teardown.description: When a worktree is removed (close, drop, release, gc, `ccp wt remove`); a failure is a warning.

up.description: `ccp wt up`: start what the worktree serves; a failure leaves it down and exits non-zero.

down.description: `ccp wt down` (and before removal of an up worktree); a failure is a warning.

urls.description: Prints a JSON list of {name, url}, any length: what the worktree serves (recorded on up; `ccp wt urls`).

merge.description: SPEC §10.5: the merge `ccp tasks close` runs; §16.5 rule 4: what does not make a head behind the tip.

command.description: A template naming {pr}, {head_sha} (required: the merge is pinned to the verified head) and {task_id}; null: gh pr merge {pr} --squash --match-head-commit {head_sha}.

behind_tip_ignore.description: Paths relative to the product root (a directory covers everything under it) whose commits on the integration tip do not make a head behind it at close or at verify launch (§16.5 rule 4).

auth_check.description: SPEC §30: auth probes the runner runs before each task (`ccp tasks claim`, `ccp auth check`).

cmd.description: Exit 0 = the credential works. Never print a secret.

allowance_stop_weekly.description: SPEC §25.3: the weekly checkpoint (percent). A new claim stops there until the lead records the operator's decision (ccp allowance continue).

session_park_pct.description: SPEC §25.4 the session park: `ccp tasks claim` and `ccp prompt` refuse (exit 6) and park the task at this 5-hour %. null: no park, no session wake, no 5-hour modelling in the forecast.

session_wake_arm_pct.description: SPEC §25.4: from this 5-hour %, `ccp allowance session-wake` tells the lead to arm a one-shot wake, and claim and prompt warn while none is armed.

session_wake_margin_s.description: SPEC §25.4: the wake (and a parked task's planned_resume_at) is the 5-hour window's reset plus this many seconds.

windows.description: SPEC §25.4 the usage windows: {<name>: {kind: weekly|session, stop_pct, park_pct}}, merged over the built-in seven_day (weekly, stop_pct = allowance_stop_weekly) and five_hour (session, park_pct = session_park_pct). The most constrained window of each kind gates.

design_seat.description: SPEC §24.5: the lead's expected model and effort. Advice only: the plane flags a difference, it never sets them.

gate.description: SPEC §14.6: the gate's time against the agent harness's foreground command limit. `ccp health` judges the latest cold run of the gate role's lane.

shell_limit_seconds.description: The harness's foreground command limit; a cold gate run above it is a health breach.

cut_line_seconds.description: The line above which the gate gets a refactor task; at most shell_limit_seconds. Null: 90% of the limit.

suite.description: SPEC §14.1: `ccp suite run`'s named lanes and its test-count pattern.

exclusive_lanes.description: SPEC §16.6: lanes that run one at a time in the queue (a run with no --lane is `full`). A run that finds one held exits 75 at once and runs nothing.

lanes.description: SPEC §14.2: a lane name to what `ccp suite run --lane NAME` runs from the checkout's root: an argv (one stage, named after the lane), or an ordered list of {name, cmd} stages, run in order until one fails. The gate role's staged lane ends with the plane's doc checks as the stage `plane-docs`.

name.description: The stage's name, unique in the lane; `plane-docs` is the plane's own.

cmd.description: A shell command, run from the checkout's root; exit 0 = the stage passed.

count_re.description: A regular expression whose first group is a test count, matched per output line and summed. Default: unittest's `Ran N tests in`.

roles.description: SPEC §14.1: the lane name the product gives each role the plane reads. Default: each role's own name.

full.description: The whole suite; a run with no --lane is this lane.

log_keep_days.description: SPEC §14.1: summary-mode logs in the queue (runs/<task>/*-suite-*.log, runs/_suite-logs/) older than this many days are removed when a `ccp suite run` starts. Default 14.

summary.description: SPEC §14.1: what `ccp suite run` reads from the output when the gate writes no result file (CCP_SUITE_RESULT, contracts/suite_result.schema.json), and what summary mode shows. Each `*_re` is a regular expression or a list of them; a key left out keeps its default (Python unittest's failures and skips; no cache counters).

failed_re.description: First group a failure count, summed. Default: unittest's `FAILED (failures=N` and `errors=N`.

skipped_re.description: First group a skip count, summed. Default: unittest's `skipped=N`.

ran_re.description: First group the units (tests, modules, files) that ran, for a product with a test cache. Default: none (set it, or write the gate's result file).

cached_re.description: First group the units the product's cache served as hits. Default: none.

cached_tests_re.description: First group the tests behind the cached units, from their last runs, recorded as cached_tests. Default: none.

section_re.description: The line after a `====` rule that starts a failing test's section. Default: `FAIL:`, `ERROR:`, `UNEXPECTED SUCCESS:`.

show_re.description: Lines shown whatever the result (at most 20). Default: none.

tail_lines.description: The log's last lines a failure shows. Default 40.

max_chars.description: The cap on what a failure shows. Default 40000.

estimate.description: SPEC §26.3: task estimation (advisory). The reference-class baseline and the estimator seat read these.

reference_since.description: Tasks merged before this date (a process change) are left out of every reference class

auto.description: Phase B: `ccp tasks check` and `ccp tasks index` start the estimator seat in the background for open tasks whose agent estimate is missing or stale (at most 10 per batch, one batch at a time). Off by default: `ccp tasks estimate --all` runs it by hand

spec_paths.description: SPEC §26.3: where the estimator looks for cited SPEC headings (globs relative to the product root, in order)

path_suffixes.description: SPEC §26.3: suffixes that make a backticked token a cited path (null: the built-in list)

review_points.description: SPEC §22: the review-point register, a product file listing each point's id (R<n>), short name, goal, status (planned|current|closed) and dates. With the file present, every review point a task, ADR, spawn or close names must be one of its ids.

file.description: The register, relative to the product root

adr.description: SPEC §6: the product's ADRs (`ccp adr`). The block is the opt-in: with it `ccp docs check` checks every ADR, the links between them, the decisions the tasks cite, and the index.

dir.description: Holds the ADRs, `NNNN-slug.md` or `<prefix>NNNN-slug.md` (ids.adr); subdirectories (an archive) included

index.description: The generated ADR index (`ccp adr index`), or null for none

transitions.description: The moves `ccp adr status` allows: a status to the statuses it may become; every name must be in `statuses`

strict.description: Turn the ADR warnings (non-canonical decision markers, missing reverse links, done tasks citing not_built decisions) into `ccp docs check` failures

template.description: A product template for `ccp adr new` (format fields id, title, title_q, date), or null for the plane's

parallel.description: SPEC §16: several tasks in flight under one runner. Absent, or max_in_flight 1: one task at a time.

max_in_flight.description: The most tasks the runner holds at once (§16.3 rule 1).

exclusive.description: Paths and globs (** spans directories) whose tasks run alone: files concurrent edits cannot be merged in safely (§16.3 rule 4).

session_ceiling_pct.description: A second task is claimed only while the account's 5-hour usage is below this (§16.3 rule 5).

ids.description: SPEC §7: the product's id and reference patterns. Every id the plane reads in the product's docs is parsed with these; an absent key keeps the default.

width.description: Digits in a task number: task files are NNNN-kebab-slug.md

prefix.description: SPEC section ref prefix: S12, S3–S5

pattern.description: Regular expression a house-rule id matches in full
Regular expression a review-point register id matches in full; its first run of digits orders the points

verify.description: SPEC §15.3: the verifier's gate. Absent, or accept_cache null: the verifier's brief is unchanged. SPEC §15.2: skip_review, the fix rounds that need no new review.

accept_cache.description: The product's content-keyed test cache stands in for a rerun: a unit (test, module or file, the product's unit) the verifier's own gate run reports as a hit on identical inputs counts as run; the gate run records ran and cached (from the gate's result file or its output's counts, §14.1), and the verify report's Suite: line ends `ran <r>, cached <c>`.

max_age_days.description: An entry older than this is no hit (the product's cache reruns it).

cold_tasks.description: Task-id globs whose gate is cold (a rollout, say), beside a task's own `gate: cold` frontmatter.

review.description: SPEC §15.3: the reviewer's touched and dependent tests may run through the same cache, a hit counting as run; its test-order and mutation runs stay uncached. Default false: the review brief is unchanged.

skip_review.description: SPEC §15.2: a fix round whose diff touches only `paths`, and that `proof` passes, goes to verify with no new review. Null: every fix round is reviewed again.

paths.description: Paths relative to the product root, as git pathspecs (a directory covers everything under it); not the root itself.

proof.description: A shell command run in the product root on the fix diff, with {task_id}, {reviewed} (the head the last review judged), {head} and {from} (the tree the fix diff starts from: the reviewed change on the head's integration base) filled in; exit 0 = the fix is proven.
